title: Cosanima MCP server + cross-harness agents (local agent tool substrate)
goal: Deliver the 1.0 agent-facing tool substrate: a local-only MCP server (`cosanima mcp`) over stdio exposing cosanima's capabilities as MCP tools and the graph/spec/plan data as MCP resources — replacing the retired 46-tool opencode suite + lib/apg.ts — plus six agents authored once in canonical markdown + YAML frontmatter with a per-harness adapter, all part of the 1.0 flag-day.

title: Local MCP server over stdio (`cosanima mcp`)
body: `cosanima mcp` runs a local MCP (Model Context Protocol) server over stdio transport — a runnable server mode of the binary, dispatched from main alongside init/scan/query/spec/plan/review. The server exposes cosanima's capabilities as MCP tools and the graph/spec/plan data as MCP resources, so any MCP-capable harness can drive cosanima. This is the agent-facing tool substrate for 1.0.

title: Local-only / private: no data leaves the host
body: The MCP server is private by construction: it binds no network sockets, speaks only stdio between the harness process and the server process on the same machine, and never transmits graph/spec/plan data off the host. There is no remote or network mode in 1.0 — local-only is a hard property, not a deployment choice.

title: MCP tools wrap the existing CLI + graph operations
body: Each MCP tool implements the same operation the corresponding CLI command does, dispatching through the same code paths (main dispatch → cmd_query / cmd_scan / spec_cmd::cmd_spec / plan_cmd::cmd_plan / review_cmd::cmd_review). The MCP surface is a protocol binding over the existing CLI + graph — not a parallel implementation — so behaviour cannot diverge between the CLI and the MCP tools.

title: Graph-query MCP tool set
body: MCP tools covering the graph lookups the retired tool suite provided: `query` (Cypher MATCH/RETURN over db.lbug, CSV result with header — the cmd_query surface), `find_symbol`, `modules`, `module_files`, `module_structs`, `file_units`, `file_path`, `methods`, `struct`, `callers`, `callees`, `uses`, `unresolved`, `hunk`. Each wraps the same graph surface the apg_* query tools did — the MCP tool set is the successor of the 46 opencode tool scripts.

title: Scan tool
body: An MCP tool wrapping `cosanima scan` end-to-end: language auto-detect (or --language/--module/--exclude-path), blacklist prefixes, the scanner + ingestor pipeline, and the .trans outputs (db.lbug + graph.jsonl + cosanima-frontend.log) — the full cmd_scan surface.

title: Spec/plan/review CRUD tools
body: MCP tools for the intent graph, mapping onto spec_cmd / plan_cmd / review_cmd: spec init/add/anchor/link/rm/render/promote/archive; plan init/add/link/done/undone/complete/render; review add/action/resolve/reject/list. Write-through semantics (JSONL first, then DB re-merge), cycle detection, and dangling-ref validation are preserved exactly.

title: MCP-native tool schemas (name + description + inputSchema + output)
body: Every tool is registered as an MCP tool schema: stable name, human-readable description, JSON input schema, and output format — declared once in the server's tool registry so harnesses discover and validate calls against the same contract. The 46 ad-hoc .ts tool definitions (and their shared lib plumbing) are replaced by these schemas.

title: Graph + spec/plan/note data as MCP resources
body: The graph and the intent graph are readable as MCP resources: graph data (db.lbug via query, or graph.jsonl) and the committed spec/note/plan JSONL (apg/specs/*.jsonl, apg/notes/<module>.jsonl, transient plans) are exposed under stable resource URIs so agents read them without shelling out. Resources mirror the on-disk layout (post-rename .cosanima/ roots).

title: Six agents authored once in canonical markdown + YAML frontmatter
body: The six agents (codebase-navigator, spec-writer, plan-writer, spec-review, plan-review, agent-builder) are authored ONCE in a canonical markdown + YAML-frontmatter form whose instructions body is harness-portable: the frontmatter carries harness-independent metadata, the body carries the full instructions. They supersede the opencode-only .opencode/agents/*.md (currently embedded via include_str! in src/main.rs ~222-247). Agent names carry the cosanima_ prefix per the rename's sweep (consumes cosanima-rename R9).

title: Per-harness frontmatter adapter (opencode / Claude Code / Codex)
body: A small per-harness frontmatter adapter renders the single canonical source into each harness's format: opencode (.opencode/agents/*.md), Claude Code (.claude/agents/*.md), Codex (.codex/agents/*.md). Only the frontmatter/format differs — the instructions body is identical in every harness.

title: Same MCP tool names across all harnesses
body: All six agents reference the SAME MCP tool names in every harness. Because the tools are MCP (harness-agnostic), no per-harness tool-syntax rewriting exists — the tool-syntax portability barrier that forced per-harness agent variants is removed.

title: Server + agents ship via the core repo; embedded tool lists removed
body: The MCP server and the cross-harness agent artifacts are 1.0 deliverables of the core repo (really-knows-ai/cosanima). The embedded include_str! tool lists in src/main.rs (lines ~28-215 — the 46 tools + lib/apg.ts) are removed/repurposed: the retired opencode tool suite is not renamed, it is gone. The agents' embedding (lines ~222-247) moves to the canonical markdown+frontmatter form.

title: `cosanima init` installs the MCP server + cross-harness agents
body: `cosanima init` installs the MCP server (registered for harness use) and the cross-harness agent artifacts instead of the opencode tool suite; the legacy-cleanup behavior (purge apg_*-named artifacts, remove pre-~/.opencode project-local installs, existing remove_legacy_project_install logic) still applies. Init converges on the cosanima layout first (consumes cosanima-rename R10).

summary: Use a Rust MCP server library (the official Rust MCP SDK or the `rmcp` crate) rather than hand-rolling the JSON-RPC/MCP protocol: the server inherits protocol correctness, transport handling, and versioning from a maintained implementation, leaving cosanima to define only its tool/resource surface.

Retire the bespoke tool layer: the 46 opencode tool scripts (apg_*.ts → would-be cosanima_*.ts) and the lib/apg.ts shared plumbing are RETIRED, not renamed — the local MCP server replaces them. This supersedes the rename's tool-suite prefix sweep (cosanima-rename R8).

Canonical-source + adapter model for agents: the six agents are authored once in canonical markdown + YAML frontmatter (harness-portable instructions body), and a small per-harness adapter emits each harness's format (opencode / Claude Code / Codex). MCP tools are harness-agnostic, so the agents reference the same tool names everywhere — markdown+frontmatter is the cross-harness agent mechanism, MCP is the cross-harness tool mechanism.

The MCP server + cross-harness agents are 1.0 deliverables: they land as part of the coordinated flag-day (parent cosanima-1.0 gates this spec), not as a post-1.0 follow-up. The tool-layer replacement is in the 1.0 cut.

Local-only stdio transport is the only server mode for 1.0: the MCP server binds no network sockets and connects to harnesses over stdio on the same machine; no data leaves the host. Privacy is a property of the design, not a deployment option.

body: No hosted or remote MCP service: the server is local-only stdio; there is no network deployment, no shared/cloud server, and no multi-tenant hosting of the cosanima MCP server for 1.0.

No general-purpose MCP broker: the server exposes only cosanima's capabilities (graph query, scan, spec/plan/review) as MCP tools + resources — there is no plugin surface for arbitrary third-party MCP tools.

The CLI is not replaced: the MCP server wraps the same operations the CLI exposes (a protocol binding, cosanima-mcp R3); the CLI remains the primary human interface, and the MCP surface introduces no separate feature set.

`cosanima mcp` starts an MCP server on stdio: an MCP client can connect, complete the initialize handshake, and list the server's tools and resources; no network socket is opened by the server process.

Every planned MCP tool (graph lookups incl. query/find_symbol/callers/callees/uses/hunk, scan, and the spec/plan/review CRUD) is registered with a stable name, description, JSON input schema, and output, and returns results equivalent to the corresponding CLI command — e.g. the query tool returns the same CSV rows as `cosanima query` on the same database.

The graph and spec/plan/note data are readable as MCP resources: a resource read returns the same content as the underlying artifact (the committed spec JSONL, notes, or the queried graph), under stable resource URIs.

The six agents render from the single canonical markdown+frontmatter source into at least opencode, Claude Code, and Codex formats via the adapter, with identical instruction bodies and identical MCP tool references in every harness.

`cosanima init` installs the MCP server + cross-harness agent artifacts and no longer installs the opencode tool-suite scripts or lib/apg.ts: a fresh init in a clean temp repo produces zero apg_* / cosanima_* opencode tool files, and legacy apg artifacts are cleaned.

Launch `cosanima mcp` and complete an MCP initialize + tools/list + resources/list exchange over a pipe with a minimal MCP client (or the MCP inspector); the server responds with the full tool and resource sets and exits cleanly on EOF.

For each MCP tool, invoke it against a fixture repo (scan it first) and diff the result against the equivalent CLI command: the query tool's CSV equals `cosanima query` output, the find_symbol/callers/callees/uses/hunk results match their CLI-backed counterparts, and spec/plan/review write tools produce the same JSONL/DB state as the corresponding CLI subcommands.

Read each resource URI through the MCP server and diff against the on-disk artifact (`.cosanima/specs/<project>.jsonl`, notes, graph query) — content matches byte-for-byte where the underlying data is deterministic.

Adapter smoke test: render the six canonical agents for the opencode, Claude Code, and Codex harness dirs and diff — the instruction bodies and every MCP tool reference are identical across harnesses; only frontmatter/format differs.

Fresh `cosanima init` in a temp repo: assert the MCP server is registered/installed and the cross-harness agent artifacts are present, and that no apg_* or cosanima_* opencode tool scripts or lib files are written; run the legacy-cleanup path against a simulated apg install and confirm apg-named artifacts are purged.

Privacy check: while the server runs with a client attached, confirm the process holds no listening sockets (lsof/netstat shows no LISTEN entries for it) and makes no outbound connections — stdio-only verified end-to-end.

Design rationale: MCP is the cross-harness TOOL mechanism; markdown+frontmatter is the cross-harness AGENT mechanism. Because cosanima's capabilities are exposed as MCP tools (harness-agnostic protocol), the six agents reference the same MCP tool names in every harness — the tool-syntax portability barrier (which forced per-harness tool wrappers) is gone. Because the agents are authored once in canonical markdown + YAML frontmatter, only a small per-harness adapter is needed to emit opencode / Claude Code / Codex formats, and the instructions body is identical everywhere. The two decisions are complementary: MCP removes tool syntax drift, the canonical source removes instruction drift.

Background — what this replaces: the current agent-facing tool layer is 46 `.opencode/tools/apg_*.ts` scripts (apg_query/scan/find_symbol/modules/module_files/module_structs/file_units/file_path/methods/struct/callers/callees/uses/unresolved/hunk + the spec/plan/review suites) plus the shared plumbing `.opencode/lib/apg.ts`, all embedded into the binary via include_str! in src/main.rs (lines ~28-215) and installed by `apg init` into ~/.opencode/, with the six agents embedded at lines ~222-247. The MCP server (cosanima-mcp) replaces the tool layer; the agents move to the canonical markdown+frontmatter form. The 46 tools are retired, not renamed (Decision D2).

Cross-spec wiring: cosanima-mcp is a child of the 1.0 flag-day (parent cosanima-1.0 SpecDependsOn cosanima-mcp — the MCP server + cross-harness agents are 1.0 deliverables, Decision D4). It SpecDependsOn cosanima-rename (it supersedes the tool-suite rename R8/R9 and rides on the init rename R10), cosanima-repo-split (the server + agents live in the core repo really-knows-ai/cosanima), and cosanima-docs (the docs must document the MCP server + cross-harness agents and stop documenting the retired tool suite as current). Requirement-level: R9 consumes cosanima-rename/R9 (agent prefix sweep), R13 consumes cosanima-rename/R10 (init convergence).
